newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE GOES BACK TO BASICS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE GOES BACK TO BASICS.

text.p: European number one Colin Montgomerie is undergoing intensive putting practise following his disastrous display in the Benson and Hedges International last weekend,
Montgomerie is determined to improve his game going into the English Open which starts on Thursday and ahead of next month's U.S. Open.

The burly Briton, who took an embarrassing five putts from inside 15 feet on the second hole of last Sunday's final round, said he has changed his putter and would also go back to a practise routine first prescribed by his college coach.

"It's a routine my coach at Houston insisted upon, taking 100 putts with 10 balls in a circle from two feet, starting all over again if you miss one," said Montgomerie, English Open winner in 1994 and runner-up in each of the past two years.
"I don't remember the last time I had to resort to this but I just wish I'd have done it last week. Then I wouldn't have five-putted in front of the Ryder Cup captain. Very embarrassing."
The day after the English Open, Montgomerie will also be playing in the Anderson Consulting World Championship in which he meets Jose Maria Olazabal in the first round.
Olazabal is seeded eighth and Montgomerie first for Monday's matchplay clash but it is the Spaniard who is the form player.
He will be looking for a good finish in the English Open to virtually seal his Ryder Cup place in only seven counting events since returning from an 18-month injury layoff.
Currently lying 11th in the European Ryder Cup standings, a 108,330 pounds ($176,000) first prize and equivalent points would leave Olazabal's place at Valderrama a formality.

"The Anderson Consulting will be a good test for me and 36 holes against Colin Montgomerie will mean I have to work very hard to get through," said Olazabal. "But I am pleased with my progress. I thought it would need much more time to shoot rounds like I've been shooting."
